papers.title: Emerging Polysaccharide-Based Biomaterials in 3D Bioprinting: Materials, Biomedical Applications, and Future Perspectives
papers.abstract: Abstract Contemporary healthcare systems require advanced, sustainable, and patient-specific therapeutic solutions. We need advanced technologies, exemplified by 3D printing and biomaterials such as carbohydrates, to produce many 3D-bioprinted in vitro tissues and organ models for drug testing and regenerative medicine. In recent years, polysaccharide-based biomaterials have emerged as promising candidates for three-dimensional (3D) printing applications owing to their intrinsic biocompatibility, biodegradability, tunable physicochemical properties, and structural resemblance to native extracellular matrices (ECMs). In addition, recent progress in biomaterial modification and 3D printing methodologies has broadened their biomedical applications, particularly in tissue engineering, regenerative medicine, organ model development for drug discovery, and in situ bioprinting. This review presents a comprehensive overview of widely utilized polysaccharides in regenerative medicine, 3D printing techniques, bioink formulations, and the biomedical applications of 3D systems. It highlights recent advancements in material design, fabrication strategies, and biological performance and addresses current challenges and future perspectives for translating these materials from laboratory research to clinical practice.

papers.title: Cation and Anion Doping in Sulfide Solid Electrolytes for All-Solid-State Lithium Batteries
papers.abstract: Compared with traditional liquid lithium-ion batteries, all-solid-state lithium batteries (ASSLBs) show great application potential. They possess better safety performance, higher energy density and adaptability to a wider range of working temperatures. Among multiple types of solid electrolytes, sulfide solid electrolytes have attracted extensive research attention. Their outstanding room-temperature ionic conductivity and great compatibility with battery electrodes make them one of the most competitive candidates. However, several inherent shortcomings still limit the practical use of sulfide solid electrolytes in high-performance batteries. Unstable interfacial chemical properties, a narrow electrochemical window, and structural damage during repeated charging and discharging cycles are the main obstacles. This review mainly focuses on the latest research progress of cation and anion doping modification strategies for sulfide solid electrolytes. By collecting and analyzing recent relevant studies, this paper summarizes the working mechanisms of different cation and anion dopants. It also compares and discusses how these doping methods affect the ionic conductivity, structural stability and interfacial compatibility of sulfide electrolytes. And in summary, the results demonstrate that rational dual doping or single doping can effectively optimize crystal lattice structure, reduce grain boundary resistance, and suppress interfacial side reactions. Appropriate doping modification significantly improves the electrochemical performance and cycling durability of sulfide electrolytes.

papers.title: The Three-Stage Trajectory of Large Language Models: 2022 to 2026
papers.abstract: This literature review puts forward a three-stage model of Large Language Models (LLMs), delineates the research goals of LLM in three stages and predicts future trends. Against the rapid, fragmented advancement of large-language-model technologies, systematic sorting of their evolutionary trajectories helps researchers grasp core contradictions and shifting research priorities. It also offers actionable reference for subsequent technical exploration, practical deployment and policy formulation in the LLM domain. In Phase 1 (2022 to 2023), LLMs have improved reasoning and general capabilities, while facing conflicts between capability and reliability. In Phase 2 (2023 to 2025), LLMs enhance evaluation and robustness, while filling the gap between benchmarks and real-world performance. In Phase 3 (2025 to 2026), LLMs improve autonomous action and safe deployment, while balancing accessibility and security. This dilemma catalyzed Phase 4 - "World Model Era", emphasizing physical simulation and causal reasoning. This work synthesizes 12 milestone papers and sorts out the development process and future trend of LLM.

llm.why_not_core: This is a literature review of LLM development stages with no RL algorithm, no world-model architecture, no engineering simulation, no FEA/surrogate modeling, and no physics-based validation.

summary_zh.validation: 无实验验证，仅文献归纳与趋势预测。

summary_en.motivation: To organize the fragmented and rapid evolution of large language models so that researchers can identify core tensions and shifting priorities.
summary_en.method: A literature review synthesizing twelve milestone papers into a three-stage evolutionary framework of LLM development.
summary_en.result: The review characterizes three phases spanning 2022 to 2026 and anticipates a subsequent world-model era centered on physical simulation and causal reasoning.
summary_en.validation: No empirical validation; the work relies solely on qualitative literature synthesis and trend forecasting.

papers.title: Mechanism, Classification and Application of Edible Bioinks for 3D Bioprinted Cultured Meat
papers.abstract: Traditional livestock farming consumes massive land and water resources while generating enormous greenhouse gas emissions, and large-scale animal slaughter also brings continuous global disputes over animal welfare and food supply security. Electrohydrodynamic three-dimensional bioprinting technology can construct highly ordered fibrous tissue structures at nanoscale precision, effectively overcoming the loose structural defects of traditional static cell scaffolds applied for cultured meat manufacturing. This paper systematically sorts current mainstream edible bioprinting raw materials into three distinct categories including plant derived, microorganism derived and synthetic composite bioinks, and fully compares their inherent printability, cell compatibility, sensory performance and existing industrial bottlenecks alongside universal material modification strategies such as physical blending and peptide grafting. Plant derived bioinks with natural fibrous architectures can well mimic the texture of native livestock meat but carry unavoidable allergen risks and unstable raw material quality. Microbial polysaccharide bioinks feature low production costs yet lack natural cell binding sites to restrict long-term myogenic maturation. Synthetic composite materials realize controllable molecular tuning, while high synthesis and purification costs limit large-scale popularization. This work establishes a multi-dimensional evaluation framework for edible bioink performance and provides systematic theoretical references for the development of low-cost, high-bionic industrial cultured meat production technologies.

papers.title: Transforming Brain Organoids Into Functional Platforms: Convergence of Engineering, Imaging, AI, and Ethics.
papers.abstract: Brain organoids are self-organizing 3D aggregates derived from pluripotent stem cells and thus mirror many aspects of human brain development, including gene expression programs, spatial organization, and neuron subtype specification. As a result, these organoids have been used to emulate neurodevelopmental, neuropsychiatric, and neurodegenerative diseases. Yet, their maturation remains fundamentally constrained by diffusion-limited necrosis, incomplete vascularization, limited visualization, and the absence of large-scale circuit integration, which collectively prevent progression beyond the fetal stage. These intrinsic limitations have catalyzed a convergence across microfluidics, biofabrication, imaging, and ethical frameworks, giving rise to a multidisciplinary movement aimed at enhancing organoid viability, reproducibility, and physiological relevance. This perspective examines how these technologies are transforming brain organoids from developmental models into experimentally robust, functional platforms.

papers.title: Synergistic photothermal and photodynamic nanocoatings on titanium implants for rapid bactericidal action and enhanced osteoinductive activity.
papers.abstract: The long-term success of titanium (Ti) implants in dental and orthopedic applications is frequently undermined by the dual challenges of interfacial infection and inadequate osseointegration. Consequently, there is an imperative need for multifunctional coatings that simultaneously exert antibacterial and osteoinductive activities. In this study, photothermal agent polydopamine (PDA) and photosensitizer rose bengal (RB) were facilely co-immobilized onto the titanium dioxide nanotube (TNT) arrays via mussel-inspired chemistry and amide coupling. This integrated platform enables highly efficient synergistic photothermal (PTT) and photodynamic (PDT) bacterial inactivation. The resulting TNT-PDA-RB nanocoating exhibited exceptional photobactericidal efficacy (>99.99%) against both Escherichia coli (E. coli) and methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) in vitro under dual-wavelength irradiation (808 nm + 532 nm) for only 3 min. Furthermore, the coating demonstrated excellent cytocompatibility with preosteoblasts and negligible hemotoxicity against erythrocytes. In vivo rat subcutaneous infection model confirms its robust anti-infective performance, achieving a bacterial load reduction of 2.49 log (>99%) compared with pristine Ti implants. Concurrently, the nanocoating significantly promoted the alkaline phosphatase (ALP) activity and the extracellular matrix (ECM) mineralization of preosteoblasts, indicating enhanced osteoinductive properties. This multifunctional TNT-PDA-RB nanocoating offers a robust and versatile strategy for augmenting the clinical performance of Ti implants.
